\par\smallskip{\footnotesize\raggedright\textit{Note.} Words: white-space tokens of the system and user messages, median over the 144 requests of a condition; rule-section words: system-message words of C1 or C2 minus those of C0 for the same case. The per-case C2 $-$ C1 difference has median 268 words (range 240--299). Validator header sentence: the first sentence of the C2 rules section, ``Review rule contracts. Each block is a rule that an independent validator will check on your output; a violated rule with onViolation=block sends the output back for repair.''; counted are requests that contain both ``an independent validator will check'' and ``sends the output back for repair''. No validation runs and nothing is sent back for repair during C2 generation (C3 is an offline validation afterwards). A key-by-key comparison of the 144/144 C0 and C5 requests finds only the top-level keys \texttt{condition}, \texttt{format}, \texttt{request\_\allowbreak{}id} different. Identical outputs: the C0 and C5 output strings of a case are byte-identical in UTF-8 (out of 144). The request files of the four generation conditions are byte-identical across the three models (first 12 hex digits of the requests SHA-256: C0 \texttt{413ef9c36e00}; C1 \texttt{05a0f21f2d1a}; C2 \texttt{9b0c6e29f8b3}; C5 \texttt{45cf0296e6a8}).\par}
